title: The Two Popes
note: "The Two Popes" - We watched "The Two Popes" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Two_Popes over the weekend. We have been exploring the way to watch a movie like a TV episode. In bits of 20-30 minutes per day. That gives us the time to talk and discuss the subject matter and doesn't keep us stuck to the sofa for long. I think it also helps to recally the story. What I loved about the movie is the expression on the Pope's face. It shows the power of words, and brilliance of the actors. Also depitcts the maturity of the Western Civilization to allow screening of the movie, without much tamasha. title: Malvani instruction to Bal Ganesha
note: I love this forward. It has been around for a while, but the way it speaks to you is so touchy. Also if you read it nicely, it gives you the opportunity to appreciate the Malvani dialect of Marathi. It’s so good.
body:
ह्या बघ आजयेच्या घराकडे जातस..नीट जा हा आणि मुख्य म्हणजे थंय गेल्यावर अजिबात मस्ती करायची नाय. एका जाग्यावर बसान रवायचा. माका कोणी विचारल्यान तर मी चवथ्या दिवशी येतलय म्हणून सांग. आजवळाक गेल्यावर नवीन वस्तू मागू नको हा, मागच्या वर्षीचा चलात म्हणून सांग हा. फक्त उगाच जास्त नको म्हणून सांग हा, ते लाड लाड करीत रवतले

निवेदाक येळ लागलो तर शांत बस हा बाबू.. आणि हा निवेदाचा ताट इल्यावर संपवून टाक हा, तू जेवच पण उंदीरमामा जेवलो काय त्यावर तूच लक्ष दि हा. परत सांगतय आजवाळचे लोक कामात असतले, तू हट्ट नको हा करु कसलो !

आरतीवाले आणि भजनावाले येतले त्या प्रत्येकाक प्रसाद आणि खावक गावला काय ता तू स्वतः बघ, घरातले गडबडीत असतले तू जरा मदत कर हा. आणि हा घरात कोण नसताना तुका बघुक पावणे इले तर त्यांच्यावर लक्ष ठेव ! तोरणाच्या ब्लपच्या जवळ जावं नको हा, आणि एकाच काडयेवर धा बारा तोरणा असतली तेव्हा जरा जपान.. आजवळाक लहान लहान बाबू असतले. त्यांच्यावर बारीक लक्ष ठेव. तुका पाया पडाक म्हणान येतले आणि फटाकरे लावक अगरबत्ती पळवन घेवन जातले. 

दिवस कमी आसतले, जो जो समोर येयत त्या प्रत्येकाचा म्हणना आयकायचा आणि ती घरात बसलेली आजी असतली तिका काम संपली की तुझ्यासमोर दोन मिनिटांसाठी वायच बस गे म्हणून बोलवन आणायचा. कशी आसस गे, दमलस काय गे, मी येव काय मदतीक असा ईचारायचा, तिका मदत लागणा नाय, पण कोणी ईचारल्यावर तिका बरा वाटता ना !

आणि हा, सगळ्यांका सांग मनापासून कायता करा, उगाच म्हागायच्या नादात पयशे सरव नको, त्यापेक्षा सगळे बोला माझ्याशी, ताच खूप हा.. तू पण प्रत्येकाशी बोल, समोरच्याक बोलतो कर..

नीट जा, येताना मी आसान पण तू येताना शिदोरी घेवन ये आठवणीन.. बाकी आमचो सगळ्यांचो लक्ष हा तुझ्यावर..फक्त दिवस उगाच लवकर सरव नको, पूरवन वापरुक सांग सगळ्यांका.. आणि हा खबरदार, जाताना बारक्यांका रडवलस तर !

जा सगळा घर तुझा हा. मठीचा देऊळ करून ये"

title: Some material to understand a bit more about data centers.
note: This is collection of information on data centers discussion. It’s a hot topic and I am sharing these so that one can a more nuanced view on the topic.
body:
Been thinking/reading a bit on the “Data Center”discussion. With 2/3 of AI built still left to be done, this has become an interesting political economy question. Every important podcast and newsletter is talking about it. 

Sharing few which I found to be very interesting. 

1. Bloomberg Odd lots - https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/odd-lots/id1056200096?i=1000784746275
2. Dwarkesh Patel approaches the data center issue from a technical standpoint. He invited Casey Handmer to his podcast - https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/dwarkesh-podcast/id1516093381?i=1000722101753 
3. Note from my colleague about one LLM query costing a water bottle led to checking these out. It doesn’t. Andy Masley - https://blog.andymasley.com/ liked his nuanced take on the podcast https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/scaling-laws/id1607949880?i=1000775770135
4. John McAuliff https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/scaling-laws/id1607949880?i=1000769054929 I liked McAuliff’s thinking on how communities can study the data centers needs and try to get deal for local communities.

title: Tukaram Mundhe and food safety
note:
Thanks to Tukaram Mundhe. One is reminded of the importance of the FDA. Google ai found some interesting facts about the same. Yes, people frequently died from eating sandwiches—and the components that went into them—before the FDA and other food regulations were established. [1, 2] 
In the 19th and early 20th centuries, before the landmark Pure Food and Drugs Act of 1906 created federal oversight, the American food supply was virtually lawless. While the term "sandwich" became popular in the late 1800s as a quick lunch for the working class, sitting down to eat one meant risking exposure to lethal bacteria, rotting meat, and toxic industrial chemicals. [2, 3, 4] 
Here is how a routine sandwich could have killed someone before regulations:
## 💀 The Bread: Toxic Fillers and Fungal Poisoning
To maximize profits, bakeries frequently stretched flour with cheaper, dangerous additives. [2, 5] 

* Chemical Adulterants: It was common to find bread whitened with alum (aluminum sulfate) or chalk, and bulked up with plaster of Paris, clay, or even sawdust.
* Ergot Poisoning: Unregulated grain harvesting meant that rye and wheat were frequently contaminated with Claviceps purpurea, a toxic fungus. Eating bread made from this grain caused ergotism (St. Anthony’s Fire), which led to gangrene, severe hallucinations, convulsions, and death.

## 🥩 The Meat: "Tubercular Beef" and Formaldehyde
Before federal meat inspections, there were no laws preventing companies from processing diseased animals. [2, 6] 

* The Preservatives: Because commercial refrigeration did not exist, meat packers kept decomposing flesh looking "fresh" by treating it with borax, lethal doses of sodium sulfite, and formaldehyde (embalming fluid) to mask the stench of rot. [2, 3, 5] 
* Diseased Livestock: As Upton Sinclair famously exposed in his 1906 novel The Jungle, scrap meat poured into sausages routinely included rats, poisoned rat bait, and meat from animals that died of tuberculosis or cholera.

## 🧀 The Cheese and Condiments: "Swill Milk" and Lead
If someone preferred a cheese or egg sandwich, the danger was just as high. [2] 

* Swill Dairy Products: In urban areas, dairy cows were kept in filthy, unventilated stables attached to whiskey distilleries and fed boiling alcohol waste ("slop"). This produced a thin, bluish, bacteria-ridden liquid known as swill milk. To make it look like thick, rich cream for cheese or butter, manufacturers added chalk, plaster, starch, and pureed calf brains. Swill dairy killed thousands of people—primarily children—every year. [2, 7, 8, 9, 10] 
* Poisonous Colors: Pickles or mustard added to a sandwich were often brightly colored using industrial dyes containing copper sulfate, lead, and arsenic. [2, 11] 

## 🔬 The Turning Point
The scale of foodborne fatalities finally led to change through the work of Dr. Harvey Washington Wiley and his famous "Poison Squad" experiments in the early 1900s, where human volunteers ingested these common food additives to document their toxic effects. Their findings horrified the public and directly prompted the creation of the agency that would become the FDA, turning the simple act of eating a sandwich from a gamble with death into a safe, everyday routine. [1, 2, 11] 
If you are interested, I can share more details about Dr. Wiley's Poison Squad or look into how the introduction of refrigeration changed food safety. What would you like to explore next?

title: LA to DC on Bike.
body:
The article about the bicycle tour of Jai Rawat and his buddies:

https://indiawest.com/three-cyclists-complete-3168-mile-ride-from-la-to-dc-in-52-days/ 

Three Cyclists Complete 3,168-Mile Ride From LA To DC In 52 Days
Three Cyclists Complete 3,168-Mile Ride From LA To DC In 52 Days
 September 24, 2026
India-West News  Desk

WASHINGTON, DC – Three Indian cyclists, Jai Rawat, 57, Anuradha Palnitkar, 54, and Samir Palnitkar, 58,  have completed a 3,168-mile ride across the United States in 52 days without a support vehicle.

The trio set out from Santa Monica Beach in Los Angeles on August 1 and reached the Washington Monument in Washington, DC, on September 21. They averaged about 65 miles a day, crossing 14 states and tackling more than 100,000 feet of climbing.

Part of the journey followed historic Route 66 before the cyclists continued east toward Washington.

The ride brought extreme heat, thunderstorms and cold weather, along with stretches of highway without shoulders and heavy truck traffic. The cyclists also had to repair their bicycles, deal with dogs chasing them and recover from cycling accidents along the way.

They crossed the Continental Divide in New Mexico at 7,881 feet and the Eastern Continental Divide in Pennsylvania at 2,392 feet.


Palnitkar became the first Indian woman to complete an unsupported, unpowered bicycle ride across the United States, according to the organizers. Rawat and Samir Palnitkar also became the first Indian Institute of Technology graduates to complete an unsupported, unpowered bicycle ride across the country.

The cyclists said the journey gave them a chance to experience small-town America and learn more about its history and communities.

“We experienced small-town hospitality as people chatted with us, offered free coffee as they learned about our cross-country ride,” Rawat said. He also recalled motorists waiting patiently behind the bicycles and shop owners sharing stories about local historical artifacts.

Rawat and Samir Palnitkar are graduates of IIT Kanpur and have been friends for 40 years. Palnitkar is a dietitian who now teaches at a special needs school. This was her first long cycle ride.

The three have trekked together in Nepal, India, Patagonia, Ecuador, France, Italy, Switzerland and Africa. Before this expedition, Rawat and Samir Palnitkar completed an 800-km bicycle ride from San Francisco to Los Angeles in 2018.US Business News

body:
दोनतीन दिवसांपूर्वी इंडियन एक्सप्रेसनं सेंट्रल सेक्रेटरियट लायब्ररीबद्दल बातमी छापली आणि लोकांना नव्या इमारतींमध्ये पुस्तकांना जागा नाही, हे कळलं. 

वास्तविक ग्रंथालयांची दुरवस्था त्यापूर्वी सुरू झाली. 

२०१५ साली नेहरू मेमोरियल लायब्ररी (आताची प्राईम मिनिस्टर्स लायब्ररी) ओखल्याला नेणार असल्याची चर्चा सुरू झाली. त्या परिसरात मोठी वृक्षतोड झाली, महागडे कॅफे आले. 

सेन्ट्रल व्हिस्टा प्रकल्प जाहीर झाल्यावर इतर ग्रंथालयांचं काय होईल, हा प्रश्न माझ्यासारख्या अनेकांना पडला. सेंट्रल व्हिस्टाची चर्चा वास्तू, खर्च, कार्यालयीन जागा, जुन्या इमारती यांच्याभोवती मर्यादित राहिली. या इमारतींमध्ये गेली अनेक दशकं साठत गेलेल्या पुस्तकांचं काय करायचं, हा प्रश्न तितकासा पुढे आला नाही.

महत्त्वाचा मुद्दा हा की, बहुसंख्य ग्रंथप्रेमी आणि अभ्यासक यांचं लक्ष्य सेंट्रल सेक्रेटरियट, नॅशनल म्युझियम, नॅशनल आर्काइव्ह, आणि IGNCA या तीन संस्थांवर केंद्रित झालं आहे. कृषी भावन, उद्योग भवन, निर्माण भवन इथली पुस्तकं, जुने दस्तऐवज यांबद्दल फारसं बोललं जात नाही. 

आता शास्त्री भवन पाडण्यासाठी इमारत रिकामी करण्याची वेळ आली असताना तिथे १९६९पासून असलेल्या ग्रंथालयाला नेमकं कुठे हलवायचं, याचं उत्तर नाही. 

सेंट्रल सेक्रेटरियट लायब्ररीची सुरुवात १८९१मध्ये कलकत्त्यात झाली. त्यावेळी सरकारी कार्यालयांमध्ये विखुरलेली सुमारे एक हजार पुस्तकं एकत्र केली होती. तेव्हा त्याचं नाव ‘इम्पिरियल सेक्रेटरिएट लायब्ररी’ होतं. ब्रिटिश भारताची राजधानी कलकत्त्याहून दिल्लीला हलवण्याचा निर्णय १९११मध्ये झाला आणि त्याबरोबर हे ग्रंथालयही दिल्लीला आलं. सुरुवातीला ते सिव्हिल लाइन्समधल्या ओल्ड सेक्रेटरिएटमध्ये गेलं. नंतर रायसीना हिलवर नवी प्रशासकीय केंद्रं उभी राहिली तेव्हा ते नॉर्थ ब्लॉकमध्ये गेलं. १९३३मध्ये नॉर्थ ब्लॉकमध्ये ते आलं आणि १९६९मध्ये नव्यानं उभ्या राहिलेल्या शास्त्री भवनच्या ‘जी’ विंगमध्ये त्याला जागा मिळाली. तेव्हापासून ते तिथेच आहे.

१९४९मध्ये युनेस्को ग्रंथालयाचा संग्रह त्यात आला. १९५०मध्ये वैज्ञानिक संशोधन आणि सांस्कृतिक व्यवहार विभागाचं ग्रंथालय त्यात आलं. अनेक व्यक्ती आणि संस्थांनी दिलेली दुर्मीळ पुस्तकंही त्यात जमा होत गेली. १ एप्रिल १९४८ला या ग्रंथालयाचं नाव केंद्रीय सचिवालय ग्रंथालय झालं. 

या ग्रंथालयात सुमारे आठ लाख पन्नास हजार दस्तऐवज आहेत. भारत सरकारचे अहवाल, राजपत्रं, सरकारी प्रकाशनं, भारतीय आणि परदेशी अधिकृत दस्तऐवज, संदर्भग्रंथ, आणि इतर पुस्तकं आहेत. मंत्रालयांच्या आणि केंद्र सरकारच्या विभागांच्या कामासाठी हे ग्रंथालय वापरलं जातं. संशोधक, विद्यार्थी आणि इतर सदस्यांनाही त्याचा वापर करता येतो.

गेली तीन वर्षं इथे अभ्यासासाठी जाणं किचकट झालं आहे. अनेक विभाग बंद असतात. कुठे डागडुजी सुरू असते. हवी ती पुस्तकं मिळत नाहीत. 

१९ फेब्रुवारी २०२० रोजी नारायणी गुप्ता यांनी इंडियन एक्स्प्रेसमध्ये लेख लिहून या आणि इतर ग्रंथालयांबद्दल चिंता व्यक्त केली. ग्रंथालयांतली पुस्तकं आणि संग्रहालयांतल्या वस्तू हलवल्यावर त्यांची देखभाल कशी करणार, त्यांना नवी जागा कोणती मिळणार, असे प्रश्न त्यांनी विचारले.  इंदिरा गांधी राष्ट्रीय कला केंद्राकडे हस्तलिखितांचे संग्रह आहेत. ही हस्तलिखितं इकडून तिकडे हलवताना नष्ट होऊ शकतात, असं त्यांचं म्हणणं होतं. १९३७साली अभिलेखागाराचा ग्रंथसंग्रह कलकत्त्याहून दिल्लीला हलवताना आणि १९८०च्या दशकात पुरातत्त्व सर्वेक्षणाच्या ग्रंथालयाचं स्थलांतर करताना काही पुस्तकं वाटेत गायब झाली होतीच.  

पुढे १२ जून २०२१ रोजी ग्रंथालय आणि माहितीशास्त्र क्षेत्रातल्या ज्येष्ठ मंडळींनी पंतप्रधानांना पत्र लिहिलं. सेंट्रल व्हिस्टामधल्या नव्या सचिवालयात सरकारी ग्रंथालयं आणि सांस्कृतिक संग्रह हलवताना योग्य नियोजन करावं, अशी त्यांची मागणी होती. त्या पत्रात दुर्मीळ पुस्तकं आणि वस्तू यांच्यासाठी हवामान नियंत्रित जागा, योग्य कपाटं, प्रशिक्षित कर्मचारी यांची व्यवस्था करावी, असं सुचवलं होतं.  ग्रंथालय कर्मचारी, अभिलेखपाल, संग्रहालय तज्ज्ञ, संवर्धनतज्ज्ञ, आणि अभ्यासक यांना एकत्र आणून स्थलांतराची योजना करावी, अशी सूचनाही केली होती. 

दरम्यान न्यू यॉर्क रिव्ह्यू ऑफ बुक्स या नियतकालिकात जगभरातल्या अनेक लेखक - इतिहासकारांनी भारतातल्या ग्रंथालयांच्या स्थलांतराबाबत काळजी व्यक्त केली. Open Letter: A Halt to New Delhi’s Demolitions असं या पत्राचं शीर्षक होतं. नमन आहुजा, अनिश कपूर, ग्लेन लोरी, ओरहान पामुक, रोमिला थापर, आणि सुसन स्ट्रॉन्ग यांच्या नावानं ते होतं. या पत्रावर जगभरातल्या सत्तरहून जास्त लेखक, कलाकार, इतिहासकार यांनी सह्या केल्या होत्या.  

याच काळात इंदिरा गांधी राष्ट्रीय कला केंद्राचं स्थलांतर सुरू झालं. सेंट्रल व्हिस्टाच्या आराखड्यात इंदिरा गांधी राष्ट्रीय कला केंद्राची जुनी जागा तीन मंत्रालयांच्या इमारतींसाठी वापरण्याची योजना होती. त्यामुळे संस्थेला तात्पुरत्या जागेत जावं लागलं. १ जुलै २०२१ला इंदिरा गांधी राष्ट्रीय कला केंद्राला जनपथ हॉटेलच्या नव्यानं तयार केलेल्या जागेत हलवलं. त्यावेळी ही जागा दोन वर्षांसाठी तात्पुरती असल्याचं सांगितलं होतं आणि पुढे जामनगर हाऊसजवळच्या जागेवर कायमस्वरूपी नवं केंद्र उभं राहणार होतं.

या केंद्रात  सुमारे तीन लाख छापील पुस्तकं, तीन लाख हस्तलिखितं, एक लाखाहून अधिक स्लाइड्स, साठ हजार मायक्रोफिल्म रोल्स, चित्रं, वस्त्रांचे नमुने आणि इतर बरंच काही होतं. यातलं बरंच सामान जनपथ हॉटेलच्या वेगवेगळ्या खोल्यांमध्ये ठेवलं गेलं. सगळं सामान तिथे पोचलं नाही, असं मी ऐकलं आहे, पण याचा पुरावा माझ्याकडे नाही.  

या स्थलांतराचं समर्थन करताना सरकारनं एक वेगळं कारण दिलं होतं. इंदिरा गांधी राष्ट्रीय कला केंद्राची मूळ इमारत प्रत्यक्षात त्याच्या ग्रंथालयासाठी बांधली होती आणि नंतर संस्थेचे बाकीचे विभाग त्यात आणले गेले होते, त्यामुळे जागा अपुरी पडत होती, असं सेंट्रल व्हिस्टाच्या अधिकृत संकेतस्थळावर सांगितलं आहे. इमारतीत पाण्याची गळती होती आणि संग्रहासाठी आधुनिक विशेष सुविधा नव्हत्या, असंही सरकारचं म्हणणं आहे. त्यामुळे नवीन इमारत आवश्यक असल्याचा दावा होता. 

हा दावा मान्य केला आणि पर्यायी जागेसाठी सावकाश का होईना, योजना तयार झाली, हे मान्य केलं तरी इतर ग्रंथालयांचा प्रश्न तसाच राहतो. 

१२ सप्टेंबर २०२३ रोजी  तत्कालीन सचिव गोविंद मोहन यांनी सचिव मनोज जोशी यांना पत्र लिहिलं आणि केंद्रीय सचिवालय ग्रंथालयासाठी नव्या केंद्रीय सचिवालयात सध्याच्या जागेइतकीच जागा द्यावी, अशी मागणी केली.

त्यांनी मागितलेली जागा होती सुमारे पाच हजार चारशे सहासष्ट चौरस मीटर. या पत्राचा उल्लेख दिल्लीहून प्रकाशित होणार्‍या टाईम्स ऑफ इंडियात आहे.  १९८४ सालापासून भारत सरकारच्या प्रकाशनांचं ‘डिपॉझिटरी’ ग्रंथालय म्हणून ते काम करत असल्यानं सेंट्रल व्हिस्टातल्या सगळ्या मंत्रालयांना आणि विभागांना ते ग्रंथालय सहज वापरता येईल, अशी जागा त्यांनी मागितली. 

पुढे दोन वर्षांनी गृहनिर्माण मंत्रालयानं कळवलं की ग्रंथालयासाठी कर्तव्य भवन नंबर दोनच्या तळमजल्यावर दोन खोल्या द्यायला मंजुरी मिळाली आहे.  या दोन खोल्यांचं एकूण क्षेत्रफळ सुमारे तीनशे चौरस मीटर होतं.

ग्रंथालयाचा सध्याचा आवाका बघता तीनशे चौ मीटर जागेत ते बसणार नाही, हे साहजिक आहे. सांस्कृतिक मंत्रालयानं तसं कळवलं. 

आता गेल्या महिन्यात इमारत पाडायची वेळ आली, तरी प्रश्न सुटलेला नाही. इंडियन एक्सप्रेसचा लेख आल्यावर नव्या इमारतीत पुरेशी जागा मिळेल, काम सुरू आहे, असं उत्तर आलं आहे. 

पण तोवर या पुस्तकांचं काय करायचं? ती कुठे ठेवायची? आणि पुरेशी जागा म्हणजे किती जागा?

तुलसी सदन लायब्ररीचा अनुभव फार जुना नाही. १९७२ साली रामचरितमानसाला चारशे वर्षं झाली, म्हणून ते सुरू झालं. सेंट्रल सेक्रेटरियट लायब्ररीची ती एक शाखा आहे.  दिल्लीच्या भगवानदास रोडवरच्या बहावलपूर हाऊसमधल्या परिसरात ते होतं. त्यात चौदा भारतीय भाषांतली दोन लाख पुस्तकं होती. २०११मध्ये मंडी हाऊस मेट्रो स्टेशनच्या बांधकामासाठी ते बंद केलं. पुस्तकं आर के पुरममधल्या एका इमारतीत हलवली. त्यानंतर  ” स्थलांतर लांबत गेलं. हे ग्रंथालय तात्पुरतं बंद असल्याचं जाहीर झालं. तीन वर्षांनी मेट्रो स्टेशन बांधून पूर्ण झालं तरी इमारत बांधली गेली नाही. आजही ते ग्रंथालय बंद आहे. 

दोन वर्षांपूर्वी आसामी आणि कन्नड विभाग सुरू झाला तो सेंट्रल सेक्रेटरियट लायब्ररीत. उरलेली पुस्तकं अजूनही आर के पुरममधल्या इमारतीत पेट्यांमध्ये ठेवलेली आहेत. 

अजून एक गंमत अशी की कर्तव्य भवनाच्या आराखड्यात इतर मंत्रालयांच्या ग्रंथालयांसाठी पुरेशी जागाच नाही. परराष्ट्र, अर्थ, गृह, ग्रामीण विकास, अवजड उद्योग इत्यादी अनेक मंत्रालयांची स्वतंत्र ग्रंथालयं आहेत. अधिकारी - संशोधक - विद्यार्थी यांना त्यांचा वापर करता येई. 

या ग्रंथालयांसाठी बारकुड्या दोनतीन खोल्या ठेवल्या आहेत. गृह आणि अर्थ मंत्रालयांचं स्थलांतर झालं तरी पुस्तकं अजून नॉर्थ ब्लॉकमध्येच आहेत. 

परराष्ट्र आणि ग्रामीण विकास या दोन खात्यांची ग्रंथालयं आता पूर्ण डिजिटल आहेत. 

या वर्षी दिल्लीत ग्रंथालयांशी संबंधित एक ज्येष्ठ अधिकारी भेटले. सरकारनं २०१६ सालापासून डिजिटायझेशन जोरात सुरू केलं आहे. लायब्ररी सायन्सचे अनेक विद्यार्थी या कामी पगारी ठेवले आहेत. लायब्रर्‍या बंद पडत असताना त्यांना हेच काम आहे. हळूहळू सगळंच ऑनलाइन आणायची सरकारची योजना आहे. 

स्कॅन करायला नेमलेले तरुणतरुणी या कामात तरबेज नाहीत, नीट स्कॅनिंग होत नाहीत, अनेक जुने कागद नष्ट होत आहेत, असं त्यांचं म्हणणं होतं. 

निधी नाही, हेही आहेच. नेहरू लायब्ररीत बॉम्बे टाइम्सची मायक्रोफिल्म बरीच नष्ट झाली. ती लंडनच्या कुठल्याश्या संस्थेनं भेट दिली होती. तिची प्रत काढा, असं कर्मचारी अनेक वर्षं सांगत होते. ते झालं नाही. आता जेमतेम तीनचार रोल शिल्लक आहेत. हेच नेटिव्ह ओपीनियनबद्दलही आहे. तिथेही स्कॅनिंग सुरू आहे. पण वर्षाला एखादं वर्तमानपत्र होतं. आणि संगणकावर ती प्रत बघणं माझ्यासारख्या अनेकांना त्रासदायक वाटतं. मायक्रोफिल्म थेट त्या काळात नेते. 

मंत्रालयांमधली पुस्तकं स्कॅन व्हायला अनेक वर्षं नक्की लागतील. शिवाय अशा संग्रहांचा सर्च नीट काम करत नाही. ऑनलाइन शोध घेणं नेहमीच सोपं नसतं. आणि सगळे दस्तऐवज स्कॅन झाले की नाही, हे कसं कळणार? स्कॅन झाल्यावर मूळ पुस्तकांचं काय करणार आहेत? डिजिटल लायब्ररी ऑफ इंडिया मूळ स्वरुपात कधीच बंद पडली. अनेक पुस्तकं कॉपीराइटच्या बाहेर नव्हती. त्या तक्रारी, खटले यांच्या नादात कॉपीराइतच्या बाहेर असलेली पुस्तकंही गायब झाली. डिजिटायझेशन केलेले अनेक संग्रह पूर्णवेळ सुरू नसतात. उदाहरणार्थ, एशियाटिक लायब्ररी. शिवाय त्यांचा सर्च ऑप्शन भंगार आहे. 

नॅशनल आर्काइव्हचा कॅटलॉग ऑनलाइन आहे. पण अनेक कागदपत्रं स्कॅन झालेली नाहीत. तिथे मुळात प्रवेशासाठी तास-दोन तास रांगेत उभं राहावं लागतं. मग स्कॅन न झालेल्या कागदांसाठी अर्ज द्यायचा. तिथे आता अभ्यासासाठी बसताच येत नाही.  

बडोद्याची हंसा मेहता लायब्ररी असो, पुण्यातलं फर्ग्युसन कॉलेज असो, किंवा इतर शेकडो लायब्रर्‍या, आपण बरीच दुर्मीळ ग्रंथसंपदा अगोदरच गमावोन बसलो आहोत. जे शिल्लक आहे, त्याचं रक्षण करायला हवं.

title: Dr. Uday Khire’s interview in BMM Vrutta — a few interesting points/TILs:
body:
Dr. Uday Khire’s interview in BMM Vrutta — a few interesting points/TILs:
1. Original interview: Dr. Gautam Pangu and Komal Kulkarni interviewed Dr. Uday Khire in the October 2026 BMM Vrutta, pp. 4–7. Khire received BMM’s 2026 Science, Technology, Education & Research Award.     BMMNewsletterOct2026docx
   BMM Vrutta — October 2026:
   https://bmmonline.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/BMMNewsletterOct2026docx.pdf
2. Pune → Nobel laureate’s lab → UC Irvine: Khire completed his PhD at CSIR-NCL, Pune. He came to the US in 1991 and did postdoctoral research at Purdue with Herbert C. Brown, winner of the 1979 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, followed by a second postdoc with Scott Rychnovsky at UC Irvine. Khire says these experiences gave him a deep grounding in complex synthetic chemistry.     BMMNewsletterOct2026docx
3. What is a kinase inhibitor? And the Nexavar connection: Kinases are enzymes involved in cellular signaling—for example, telling cells when to grow or divide. In some cancers, these signaling pathways become abnormally activated. Kinase inhibitors are targeted drugs designed to interfere with these signals. Khire spent about 11 years at Bayer working in cancer drug discovery, including on a B-Raf kinase inhibitor that progressed from preclinical development to clinical trials and eventually became an approved drug.     BMMNewsletterOct2026docx Patent records connect Khire’s Bayer work to sorafenib (Nexavar); he is a named inventor on relevant Bayer RAF-kinase patents.
4. An interesting, though indirect, connection to Katalin Karikó: Karikó’s breakthrough involved making therapeutic mRNA work effectively in cells, while Khire’s work has largely involved small-molecule medicinal chemistry and kinase inhibitors. These are different technologies, so there isn’t a direct research connection. But there is a broader conceptual connection: both involve understanding molecular machinery inside cells well enough to intervene selectively and turn that knowledge into medicines.
5. What comes next is perhaps even more interesting: Khire’s Pune lab is now researching proximity-induced protein degradation. Instead of merely blocking a disease-causing protein, the idea is to harness the cell’s own machinery to degrade and remove the protein itself. Khire also makes an interesting observation about India: Pune/NCL provides excellent scientific talent, but funding innovative drug discovery remains challenging because India’s VC ecosystem is still developing. title: *नको मत्स्यगंधा*
body:
*नको मत्स्यगंधा*

इथेच ह्या तीरावर
भेटली ती एकदा
निसटली ह्या हातांतून
माझी ती मत्स्यगंधा

पाणीदार डोळे निळे
खवल्यांसम केस कुरळे
गतजन्मीची मासळीच
माझी ती मत्स्यगंधा

अथांग ह्या सागरात
असतीलही परी अनेक
तिच्यासारखी तीच एक
माझी ती मत्स्यगंधा

पहाटेस रोज रोज
पुसतसे मी “भास्करा,
दिसली का रे आज तूज 
माझी ती मत्स्यगंधा?”

विचारात धुंद तिच्या
वाट हरवलो एकदा
मिळेल तरी कशी तेथे
माझी ती मत्स्यगंधा?

भेटल्या परी तेथे मज 
कुंदा जुई सुगंधा, अन 
विसरलो मी त्या भानात
कशी कोण मत्स्यगंधा

आठवण ती दडपून आता
भटकतो मी सर्वदा
थांबव शोध तू ही भास्करा
नकोच ती मत्स्यगंधा

नितिन हे. वैद्य

ज्ञानेश्वरीः

title: सेप्टोलेसेंट म्हणजे काय? - मराठी अनुवाद
body:
सेप्टोलेसेंट म्हणजे काय? - मराठी अनुवाद

"सेप्टोलेसेंट" हा शब्द ७० वर्षांपेक्षा जास्त वय असलेल्या, पण तरीही किशोरवयीन मुलासारख्या उत्साहाने आणि ऊर्जेने जगणाऱ्या व्यक्तीसाठी वापरला जातो.

"सेप्टो" म्हणजे सात, जो ७०+ वय दर्शवतो, तर "अ‍ॅडोलेसेंट" म्हणजे किशोरवयीन.

सेप्टोलेसेंट म्हणजे अशी व्यक्ती जी ७० वर्षे पूर्ण केल्यानंतरही किशोरवयीन मुलाच्या उत्साहाने आयुष्य जगते.

साधारणपणे ७० ओलांडल्यानंतर काही लोक विचार करतात,
"मी आता म्हातारा झालो;
माझे आयुष्य संपत आले आहे."
पण सेप्टोलेसेंट असा विचार करत नाही. ते वयाला फक्त एक आकडा समजतात आणि जणू नवीन प्रकरण सुरू करत असल्यासारखे आयुष्याला सामोरे जातात.

अशा लोकांची १० सोपी वैशिष्ट्ये:

ते नेहमी स्वतःला व्यस्त ठेवतात:
ते फक्त घरी बसून टीव्ही बघत नाहीत. ते काहीतरी अर्थपूर्ण कामात गुंतलेले असतात, जसे की काम करणे, पुस्तक लिहिणे, बागकाम करणे किंवा कोणाला तरी शिकवणे.

ते मैत्री जपतात:
ते स्वतःला एकटे पाडत नाहीत. ते किमान तीन चांगल्या मित्रांना भेटण्यासाठी वेळ काढतात, एक कप कॉफीचा आनंद घेतात आणि गप्पा मारतात.

त्यांना प्रवास करायला आवडतो:
ते पंचतारांकित हॉटेलमध्ये राहण्याचा आग्रह धरत नाहीत. बसमधून का होईना, पण नवीन ठिकाणी प्रवास करण्यात त्यांना आनंद मिळतो. त्याचबरोबर त्यांना चांगले जेवण आणि छान कपडे घालायलाही आवडते.

ते नातेसंबंध जपतात:
ते जोडीदार, मुले आणि नातवंडांसोबत प्रेमळ नाते टिकवून ठेवतात. प्रत्येकाने त्यांच्याशी सहमत व्हावे किंवा त्यांच्या इच्छेनुसार वागावे असा आग्रह ते धरत नाहीत.

त्यांचे नेहमी एक नवीन ध्येय असते:
ते स्वतःसाठी लहान-लहान ध्येये ठरवतात, जसे की या महिन्यात एक पुस्तक वाचणे किंवा एक झाड लावणे. ते आयुष्य कधीही पूर्णपणे रिकामे होऊ देत नाहीत.

ते आरोग्याची काळजी घेतात:
ते आजारी पडल्यावर घाबरत नाहीत किंवा प्रत्येक गोष्टीला म्हातारपणाचे कारण म्हणून सोडून देत नाहीत. ते दिवसातून किमान २० मिनिटे चालणे आणि निरोगी अन्न खाणे यांसारख्या सवयींमधून त्यांच्या आरोग्याला प्राधान्य देतात.

ते छोट्या-छोट्या गोष्टींमध्ये आनंद शोधतात:
ते नेहमी मोठ्या यशाचा किंवा इच्छांचा पाठलाग करत नाहीत. नातवंडाचा वाढदिवस, एखादा छान टीव्ही कार्यक्रम किंवा सकाळचे कोवळे ऊन यात त्यांना आनंद मिळतो.

ते कृतज्ञतेने जगतात:
त्यांच्याकडे जे नाही त्याबद्दल सतत तक्रार करण्याऐवजी, त्यांच्याकडे जे आहे त्याबद्दल ते कृतज्ञ असतात. चांगले जेवण यासारख्या रोजच्या आशीर्वादासाठी ते देवाचे आभार मानतात आणि इतरांना मदत करतात.

ते नेहमी हसतमुख असतात:
ते चेहऱ्यावर कपाळावर आठ्या घेऊन फिरत नाहीत. ते आनंदी वृत्ती ठेवतात आणि इतरांनी दुर्लक्ष केलेल्या छोट्या फुलातही आनंद शोधतात.

ते आहे त्यात समाधानी असतात:
आपल्याकडे लाखो रुपये नाहीत म्हणून ते दुःखी होत नाहीत. त्याऐवजी ते विचार करतात, "माझ्याकडे माझे आरोग्य, माझे कुटुंब आणि माझा आनंद आहे. मी आयुष्याच्या खऱ्या अर्थाने आधीच करोडपती आहे."

"आपण वृद्ध होणे थांबवू शकत नाही, पण ते वृद्धत्व किती सुंदरपणे, सन्मानाने आणि आनंदाने जगायचे हे मोठ्या प्रमाणात आपल्याच हातात आहे."

म्हातारपण आल्यावर आपण दि ववस दुःखी होऊन अंथरुणाला खिळून घालवायचे, की हसत-हसत, लोकांशी जोडलेले राहून आणि अर्थपूर्ण कामात गुंतून राहायचे?

निवड आपलीच आहे ! ‎

title: How Tos for creating a linked blog
note: Agent friendly guide on creating a linked blog. The idea is from Simon Willison.
body:
Help me build my own WhatsApp-powered archive and link blog

I am not technical. Work with me step by step to build and operate this. Explain unfamiliar terms in plain English, ask only the questions needed for the next step, and do the implementation yourself wherever your tools allow.

Example of the experience I want:
https://priyaranjanmarathe.github.io/finds/

Use this website as a reference for the user experience only. Build an independent implementation for my accounts. Do not inspect, copy, or depend on its owner’s source repository, code, credentials, or infrastructure.

What I want

I receive useful links, messages, photos, videos, audio, and documents on WhatsApp. I want to forward selected items to a dedicated WhatsApp number, then choose which ones to publish to my own searchable GitHub Pages website.

This should process only what I deliberately send to that number. It should not require access to my existing chats, contacts, or groups.

My everyday workflow

1. I forward an item to the dedicated number.
2. I reply directly to that item with a command such as:

save #books #science
Title: An interesting discovery
Note: My commentary on why this is worth keeping.

3. The selected item appears on my website after processing.

Require a direct reply so the system knows exactly which item I selected. Never guess the target from nearby messages. Forwarding something alone must not publish it.

Let me revise titles, notes, and tags, and remove published items. Explain the supported commands and any time limits. If an old post can no longer be edited through WhatsApp, provide a simple alternative.

Website requirements

* Newest posts first, with a permanent link to each post.
* Titles, original text or links, my commentary, dates, and clickable tags.
* Full-text search and tag filtering.
* Images and appropriate audio/video players or document links.
* A mobile-friendly layout with readable Marathi, Hindi, and English.
* Clear handling of unsupported or oversized attachments.
* Exportable records so I can move my archive later.

Privacy and publication

Explain the difference between a private archive and a public website before setup. Ask me to confirm which content I want public. Do not describe a public GitHub Pages site as private storage.

Keep unselected messages, sender numbers, credentials, and internal inbox data out of the public repository and website. Warn me that selected messages and attachments may themselves contain personal information.

Explain what removing a post does—and what may remain in Git history, attachment storage, caches, or downloaded copies.

How to work with me

Start by asking:

* What computer do I use, and what agent tools are available?
* Do I already have GitHub and Meta accounts?
* Do I have a suitable WhatsApp number for this setup?
* What should the website be called?
* What monthly budget am I comfortable with?

Recommend the simplest maintainable architecture. GitHub Pages should host the website; use suitable services for receiving WhatsApp messages, keeping the inbox private, and storing public attachments. Explain the role of Meta’s WhatsApp Cloud API and whether Vercel, Cloudflare, or another service is needed.

Check current official documentation before giving account instructions, pricing, or platform restrictions. Explain test-number limitations, production requirements, token expiry or revocation, storage and bandwidth limits, and possible charges. Do not assume everything is free or that paid AI subscriptions are required.

Give me one manageable setup step at a time. When I must sign in, verify a number, approve access, or configure a secret, tell me exactly what to do. Never ask me to paste passwords or access tokens into chat. Store credentials using the appropriate platform’s secret settings.

Security and reliability

Verify incoming webhook signatures and accept messages only from my authorized sender number. Protect the private inbox, prevent duplicate posts on retries, retry failed imports, and avoid logging private content or credentials.

Set a clear retention period for unselected messages. Make publication failures visible to me without exposing private data.

Explain the expected publishing delay. Scheduled processing is acceptable; include a manual way to run it.

Completion and handoff

Implement the complete flow and test it with my permission using deliberately chosen sample content:

* A text/link post.
* An image post.
* An update to a published post.
* Removal of a test post.
* An unselected message that must remain unpublished.
* A repeated delivery that must not create a duplicate.

Show me the actual published results and report anything that remains untested.

Finish with short instructions covering how to save, edit, remove, search, export, and troubleshoot. Record which accounts and services I own, where settings are managed, and what maintenance may be needed—without including secret values.

Begin by checking my starting setup and guiding me through the first step.

body: Sixteen U.S. vice presidents, from Harry Truman through Kamala Harris. Six became President, four won the nomination but lost the election, and six were never nominated. Explore the interactive story below.

Republican VPs, by contrast, mostly never got the nomination at all: five of the six “never nominated” names are Republicans. (The one wrinkle in that clean line: Richard Nixon did lose a general election as the nominee, in 1960 — but he came back and won in 1968, so his final outcome is President.) 04How the six got there Even among the six who made it, half never won the office as a vice president running for promotion — they inherited it mid-term. Truman, Johnson, and Ford were already president when they won (or, in Ford's case, lost) their elections; Nixon waited eight years and Biden four. The “VP as heir apparent” story is mostly a story about succession and comebacks, not coronations. 05The Biden wrinkle Counting rule that matters Not the nominee in 2016 — President anyway If you counted only the immediate post-VP cycle, Joe Biden would look like a miss: in 2016 he didn't run at all, and Hillary Clinton took the Democratic nomination. But the count here is about final outcomes, not first cycles. In 2020 Biden won the nomination and the presidency — so he belongs with the six who made it, not the ten who didn't. 2009–17Vice president under Barack Obama, two terms → 2016First post-VP cycle: doesn't run; Clinton is the nominee → 2020Runs, wins the nomination, wins the presidency He's not the only delayed case, either — Nixon lost in 1960 and won in 1968. What makes Biden unique in the sixteen is that he skipped his first cycle altogether and still came back to win, which is exactly why he stays out of the “never became President” count. How this was counted Distinct individuals who served as vice president from the end of World War II onward, starting with Harry Truman (who took the office in January 1945) and ending with Kamala Harris. Each person is counted once, by final outcome, regardless of how many cycles they contested. JD Vance is excluded because his post-vice-presidency cycle has not yet occurred. Outcomes: became President (by succession or election, at any point); nominated, lost (won a major-party presidential nomination and lost the general election, and never became President); never nominated (never won a major-party presidential nomination). Richard Nixon lost the 1960 general election as the Republican nominee before winning in 1968; he is counted by his final outcome, as President.

मराठी रंगभूमी दिन  ५ नोव्हेंबर

रंगभूमी म्हणजे आपल्या संस्कृतीचा, संवेदनांचा आणि समृद्ध कलापरंपरेचा जिवंत आरसा. रंगमंचावर पडदा उघडतो, दिव्यांचा प्रकाश पसरतो आणि काही क्षणांत आपण वास्तवाच्या जगातून भावनांच्या एका वेगळ्याच विश्वात प्रवेश करतो. कधी हसवणारी, कधी रडवणारी, कधी अंतर्मुख करणारी, तर कधी जगण्याचा नवा अर्थ सांगणारी ही रंगभूमी माणसाच्या मनाशी थेट संवाद साधते.

या रंगभूमीला समृद्ध करणारे असंख्य नाटककार, लेखक, दिग्दर्शक, अभिनेते, अभिनेत्री, संगीतकार, नेपथ्यकार, प्रकाश योजनाकार, रंगभूषाकार, वेशभूषाकार, तंत्रज्ञ आणि पडद्यामागे अहोरात्र मेहनत करणारे सर्व कलावंत यांना मनापासून वंदन. "पडेल ते काम आणि कमी तिथे आम्ही" या तत्वावर अनेक रंगभूमीची अविरत सेवा करताना दिसतात त्यांनाही मनापासून दंडवत.

कितीतरी कलाकारांनी आपले संपूर्ण आयुष्य या कलेसाठी समर्पित केले. टाळ्यांच्या गजरात मिळणारा आनंद अनुभवला, तर कधी प्रयोग संपल्यानंतरच्या नीरव शांततेत पुढच्या प्रयोगाची स्वप्ने पाहिली. त्यांच्या कष्टातूनच मराठी रंगभूमीचा हा वैभवशाली प्रवास घडला आहे.

आज मनोरंजनाची अनेक आधुनिक माध्यमे आपल्या समोर असली, तरी प्रत्यक्ष रंगमंचावर कलाकाराचा जिवंत अभिनय अनुभवण्याची सर कोणत्याही माध्यमाला येऊ शकत नाही. आणि म्हणूनच ‘डिजिटल वॉल’ या आधूनिक बॅकड्रॉपचे प्रलोभन असले तरी ते जिवंत कलेसमोर फिके पडते. एका प्रसिद्ध नेपथ्यकाराबरोबर या संदर्भात चर्चा झाली होती, तो म्हणाला “जो पर्यंत नाटक ही कला रंगमंचावर सादर होतेय तिथे नेपथ्य, सेट, प्रकाश योजना, प्रॉपर्टी, एंट्री आणि एक्झिट या गोष्टींना पर्याय नाही. प्रत्येक नाटकाचा सेट हे एक पात्र असतं आणि सेट सुद्धा नाटकात जिवंतपणा घेऊन येतो”. स्वत: एक उत्तम वास्तुविशारद (Architect) असल्यामुळे पुढे असंही म्हणाला एक दिवस असा येईल की नाटकाच्या सेट मधील प्रत्येक स्टेज फ्लॅट हा एक डिजिटल स्क्रीन असेल पण त्याला काही अर्थ उरणार नाही आणि नाटकातील जिवंतपणा निघून जाईल.

नाटक केवळ पाहिले जात नाही, ते जगले जाते, अनुभवले जाते आणि मनाच्या खोल कप्प्यात कायमचे जपले जाते. रंगभूमी ही केवळ कला नाही, ती एक संस्कारशाळा आहे. ती विचार देते, संवेदना जागवते आणि माणूस म्हणून अधिक समृद्ध करते.

नाटक म्हणजे अभिनयाचा आणि शब्दांचा प्रवास. त्यात शब्दांना महत्व अधिक. भारतीय तत्त्वज्ञानानुसार वाणीचे परा, पश्यंती, मध्यमा आणि वैखरी असे चार स्तर मानले गेले आहेत. नाटक आणि अभिनयाच्या प्रक्रियेशी त्यांचा थेट संबंध दिसून येतो. परा वाणी ही भावनेची सर्वांत सूक्ष्म अवस्था आहे. संवाद उच्चारण्यापूर्वी पात्राच्या मनात जी मूलभूत भावना किंवा प्रेरणा निर्माण होते, ती परा वाणीशी संबंधित असते. पश्यंती वाणीत या भावनेला अंतर्मनात प्रतिमा मिळते जिथे अभिनेता/अभिनेत्री प्रसंग, व्यक्ती आणि अनुभव मनात पाहू लागतो. त्यामुळे त्यांच्या अभिनयाला भावनिक सत्यता मिळते. मध्यमा वाणी ही अंतर्गत विचारांची अवस्था आहे. संवाद बोलण्यापूर्वी त्याचा अर्थ, हेतू, भाव, विराम आणि कोणत्या शब्दावर भर द्यायचा हे अभिनेत्याच्या मनात घडत असतं. आणि अर्थात वैखरी वाणी म्हणजे प्रत्यक्ष उच्चारलेला संवाद. आवाज, स्वर, लय, शब्दोच्चार, गती आणि संवादफेक यांच्या माध्यमातून विचार व भावना प्रेक्षकांपर्यंत पोहोचतात. म्हणूनच प्रभावी अभिनय केवळ संवादफेकीवर अवलंबून नसतो. अभिनेता आधी अनुभवतो, मग मनात पाहतो, विचार करतो आणि शेवटी बोलतो. या चारही स्तरांचा समन्वय झाला तर संवाद केवळ ऐकू येत नाही, तर तो प्रेक्षकांच्या मनाला स्पर्श करतो. मराठी रंगभूमी ही या सर्व अवस्थेतून परिपक्व झालेली आहे.

५ नोव्हेंबर १८४३ रोजी सुरु झालेला हा प्रवास गेली १८३ वर्ष अखंड आणि अविरत सुरुच आहे. आपण स्वा. सावरकरांचे ऋणी असायला पाहीजे त्यांनी हा दिवस "मराठी रंगभूमी दिन" म्हणून साजरा व्हावा यासाठी अथक प्रयत्न केले व ते १९४३ साली शताब्दी महोत्स्वाच्या निमित्ताने मान्य झाले.

मराठी रंगभूमीचा हा समृद्ध वारसा असाच पुढे जात राहो. नव्या पिढीला रंगभूमीचे आकर्षण वाटो, नवे प्रयोग घडोत आणि नाट्यरसिकांच्या मनातील नाटकाविषयीचे प्रेम सदैव जिवंत राहो.

मराठी रंगभूमीला मानाचा मुजरा.

रंगभूमीवर प्रेम करणाऱ्या प्रत्येक कलावंताला आणि रसिकाला मनःपूर्वक शुभेच्छा!!

मिलिंद प्रधान

title: Marathon Safety Data Story
body: What 29.3 million US race finishes tell us about cardiac arrests, survival and the limits of comparing race-day risk with long-term running benefits. Explore the corrected interactive story below.

embedded_story.title: Marathon Safety Data Story: Run for Your Life

search_text: Run for Your Life — What the Data Says About Marathon Deaths Hyderabad · Research A data story about running and risk Run for your life — what the data says about risk. According to local reports citing police, Kommineni Gopi , a 36-year-old software engineer with IBM, died minutes after finishing the Hyderabad Hi-Tech Full Marathon on Sunday, 1 November 2026 — he had crossed the line at Gachibowli Stadium, collected his finisher's medal, and collapsed walking toward breakfast. His death is a tragedy, and it is also the kind of headline that makes millions of runners quietly wonder whether the sport they love is dangerous. So we put the headline next to a large US registry addressing race-associated cardiac arrest — the RACER registry's analysis of 29.3 million race finishes (Kim et al., JAMA 2025) — and this is what it actually shows. The short version: race-associated cardiac death is rare, but the risk is not zero . In two US registry periods, its rate fell from 0.39 to 0.20 per 100,000 race finishes. Separately, regular running is associated with longer life. That does not establish that running a marathon is safer than not entering one. What happened Sunday morning in Hyderabad Kommineni Gopi , 36, was a software engineer with IBM and, in the words of those close to him, a fitness enthusiast. Originally from Ravinuthala village in Khammam district, he had settled in Hyderabad with his family — at Alkapur Colony in Manikonda. On 1 November 2026 he ran the 8th edition of the Hyderabad Hi-Tech Full Marathon at Gachibowli Stadium. He did the hardest part. Then, minutes after it was over, he died. The race 42.2 km, completed Gopi ran the full marathon at Gachibowli Stadium and crossed the finish line. Minutes later Medal collected, then collapse He collected his finisher's medal and was walking toward the breakfast area when he collapsed. On the spot CPR by the organising team Members of the organising team gave him CPR where he fell, before he was moved to a nearby private hospital in Gachibowli (reported as CARE Hospital). ~8:45 AM Declared dead at hospital Doctors declared him dead at around 8:45 am. Afterwards Cause not yet confirmed Gachibowli police said preliminary information suggests a heart attack; a post-mortem examination was initiated to establish the exact cause. A reported collapse is not a confirmed diagnosis. Contemporary news reports say Gopi collapsed after finishing. They do not establish his underlying medical condition. Cardiac arrest means the heart has stopped pumping effectively; a heart attack is one possible cause, not a synonym. The registry below tracks cardiac arrests during races and up to an hour afterwards. His death has shaken Hyderabad's running community and put medical screening and emergency support at mass-participation races back in focus. Our thoughts are with his family, his friends, and everyone who ran alongside him on Sunday. His story deserves care; population data can add context without explaining an individual death. The denominator One death is a tragedy. 29.3 million finishes are the context. News reports count deaths one at a time, with no denominator. The Race Associated Cardiac Event Registry (RACER) counts both. In March 2025, Jonathan H. Kim of Emory University and colleagues published a new registry analysis in JAMA : cardiac arrests identified through systematic surveillance at US marathons and half-marathons from 2010 to 2023, set against every finisher. 29.3M Race finishes — 29,311,597 marathon and half-marathon finishers in the US, 2010–2023. This counts finishes, not unique people; one runner may enter many races. 176 Cardiac arrests in all those races over 14 years — about 1 in every 166,500 finishes . 66% Survived. 117 of 176 people with a recorded cardiac arrest survived to hospital discharge (66%), compared with 29% in the earlier registry. In rate terms: 0.60 cardiac arrests per 100,000 race finishes , and 0.20 cardiac deaths per 100,000 — one death per roughly 500,000 finishes. To feel what that means at the scale of a single race, use the explorer below. Every figure comes from Kim et al., JAMA 2025. The risk explorer: who, and which race? Cardiac arrests per 100,000 race finishes, RACER 2010–2023. Pick a group — the bars keep every group on the same scale so you can compare honestly. All runners Marathon Half-marathon Men Women 0.60 cardiac arrests per 100,000 race finishes ≈ 1 arrest per 166,700 finishes Scaled to one million race finishes, the study rates correspond to about 6 arrests, 4 survivors and 2 deaths . These are population averages, not individual predictions. Men 1.12 Marathon 1.04 All runners 0.60 Half-marathon 0.47 Women 0.19 The trend Similar arrest rates. A roughly halved cardiac death rate. The two registry reports found similar overall cardiac arrest rates: 0.54 and 0.60 per 100,000 race finishes. The cardiac death rate fell from 0.39 to 0.20 per 100,000. This is a comparison between study periods, not evidence that risk falls every year. The original report covered 2000 through May 2010; the later report covers 2010–2023. The 2025 paper labels its historical comparator “2000–2009”; the button below gives the date range stated in the original 2012 report. 2000–May 2010 · RACER 1 2010–2023 · RACER 2 Cardiac arrests / 100k 0.54 59 arrests among 10.9 million race finishes. Cardiac deaths / 100k 0.39 The arrest, too often, was the end of the story. Of cardiac arrest cases, died 71% 42 of 59 cardiac arrest cases were fatal. Of cardiac arrest cases, survived 29% Survival was the exception, not the rule. Why did survival improve? The authors point to rapid CPR, AED access and emergency planning as plausible contributors. Detailed clinical and emergency-response information was available for only 36 cases, so the registry cannot prove how much each change caused the improvement. The practical lesson is to prepare for a fast response along the whole course and at the finish. The pattern inside the rarity Rare everywhere — but not evenly rare A rate of 0.60 per 100,000 is an average over very different runners and very different miles. In the 2010–2023 report: ~6× Men vs women: 1.12 arrests per 100,000 male finishes vs 0.19 per 100,000 female finishes. Sex was known in 146 of 176 cases: 127 men and 19 women; 30 were unknown. The published rates account for missing data using imputation. ~2.2× Marathon vs half: 1.04 per 100,000 in the full marathon vs 0.47 in the half. The observed marathon rate was about 2.2 times the half-marathon rate. This does not isolate the effect of distance from differences between runners or events. 40% Coronary artery disease was the most common identified cause: 27 of 67 cases with an established cause, about 40%. A cause was known for only 67 of the 176 arrests, so this is not 40% of all cases. Schematic of a marathon course, not a measured distribution of arrests. 0 – 10.5 KM Settling in 10.5 – 21 KM Cruising 21 – 31.5 KM The grind 31.5 – 42.2 KM Final quarter Late-race and finish areas deserve particular emergency-response attention Race-associated cardiac arrests often cluster in the final quarter and near the finish . This supports strong medical and AED coverage there, alongside a rehearsed response throughout the course. These data do not establish that a finishing sprint or an abrupt stop causes the pattern. The exercise paradox Yes, the risk spikes during a run. That's only half the sentence. The exercise paradox is that vigorous exertion can briefly raise cardiac-event risk, especially in susceptible people, while regular physical activity supports long-term cardiovascular health. Siscovick and colleagues ( NEJM , 1984) studied men without known heart disease. Their historical estimates were: 56× Relative risk of cardiac arrest during vigorous exercise for men who were usually sedentary compared with the same group at other times. 5× The same during-exercise spike for men who exercised vigorously habitually . The exertion-related relative risk was much smaller in this group, but this was not a randomized training trial. 0.4× The habitual exercisers' overall risk of cardiac arrest — during exercise and at rest combined — was just 40% of the sedentary men's . These historical relative risks are not an individual's chance of dying, and they cannot diagnose what happened to Gopi. A race can trigger an event in someone with an underlying condition, but neither fitness nor a lack of symptoms guarantees protection. Regular activity, gradual preparation and attention to warning symptoms are more useful takeaways than treating a marathon as a medical stress test. The other side of the ledger What long-term running studies show Not running is not the same as being inactive: walking, cycling and other activities also count. Lee and colleagues ( Journal of the American College of Cardiology , 2014) followed 55,137 adults for an average of 15 years. After adjustment for measured differences, runners had these associations compared with non-runners: Lower observed all-cause mortality −30% Bar shows runners' risk relative to non-runners = 100%. Lee et al., JACC 2014. Lower observed cardiovascular mortality −45% An observational association, not proof that running itself caused the whole difference. Longer life expectancy +3 years Estimated difference between runners and non-runners in this cohort, not a guaranteed gain for an individual. And it isn't one study standing alone. Pedisic and colleagues' meta-analysis ( British Journal of Sports Medicine , 2020) pooled 14 reports from six prospective cohorts with 232,149 people and found running associated with 27% lower all-cause mortality, 30% lower cardiovascular mortality, and 23% lower cancer mortality than not running. These observational studies cannot rule out residual confounding or establish the extra benefit of marathon racing. In Lee's data, the association appeared at much smaller amounts than marathon training: Running even 5–10 minutes a day, at a slow pace under 6 mph , was associated with meaningfully lower risk. There is no need to enter a marathon to be physically active. Scale it to a race you might actually run Using RACER 2's combined rates for marathons and half-marathons (0.60 arrests and 0.20 deaths per 100,000 finishes), here is what a field of finishers statistically "expects." These are averages across many races — most individual races see none at all. 25,000 finishers 0.15 expected cardiac arrests across a field this size — roughly one arrest in every 7 races of this size . 0.05 expected cardiac deaths — roughly one death in every 20 races of this size . These figures do not count every other medical emergency, injury or non-finisher. For historical context, Dan Tunstall Pedoe reported about one cardiac death per 80,000 completed runs across roughly 650,000 London Marathon finishes in 1981–2006. That single-marathon series is not directly comparable with the later US registry, which is mostly half-marathon finishes. Within the US reports, survival after cardiac arrest improved; the newer survival figure refers to cardiac arrest, not to every type of race emergency. What the data asks of you Not "don't run." Run like the numbers are watching. Low population risk is not a reason for complacency, and it does not determine any one person's risk. The evidence points to a short, concrete list: 01 Build gradually; arrive trained The during-exercise spike is largest in people unaccustomed to vigorous effort (56× in Siscovick's sedentary group vs 5× in the habitually active). Build exercise intensity and duration gradually; avoid a sudden jump into strenuous exercise. 02 Know your family history — and say it out loud Early heart disease in close relatives, unexplained fainting, or a family death at a young age are reasons to talk to a doctor before a first marathon, not after a scare. 03 Treat symptoms as data, not weakness Stop exercising and seek medical attention for chest pain or pressure, unusual breathlessness, dizziness, fainting or concerning palpitations. Severe or persistent symptoms call for emergency help. Do not train or race through them. 04 Respect the last quarter — and the finish Arrests often occur late in a race, but warning symptoms matter at any point. Stop and alert the medical team rather than merely slowing down or trying to reach the line. 05 Don't race sick, and don't debut at 42.2 km on a dare Do not race with a fever or when acutely unwell; seek medical advice when needed. Choose a distance suited to your training. The lower average arrest rate in half-marathons is not a personal safety guarantee. 06 Learn CPR. You are the intervention. If someone is unresponsive and not breathing normally, summon emergency help, start CPR and get an AED. Follow its prompts. CPR/AED training can help you respond; it cannot guarantee survival. A note on screening: Discuss symptoms, existing conditions and a family history of premature heart disease or sudden death with a qualified clinician, especially before a major increase in exercise. Screening cannot detect every condition or guarantee safety; the right assessment depends on the individual. Organizers also need a rehearsed emergency plan, trained responders and accessible AEDs. The verdict Keep running in perspective. Take symptoms seriously. Kommineni Gopi's death is a human loss, not a statistic to explain away. The population evidence still matters: race-associated cardiac death was rare in this US registry, and most people with a recorded arrest survived. Separately, habitual running was associated with lower long-term mortality. Neither result tells us why he died or guarantees that a marathon is safe for a particular runner. Enjoy physical activity, build gradually, pay attention to symptoms and choose events with sound medical preparation. You do not need 42.2 kilometres to gain from an active life. For personal risk or medical clearance, talk with a qualified clinician. Sources & method The Hyderabad report — Kommineni Gopi's death as given in the news item this story is built on, cross-checked against Telangana Tribune and Hyderabad Mail (hospital named as CARE Hospital; cause awaiting post-mortem). Kim JH, Rim AJ, Miller JT, et al. "Cardiac Arrest During Long-Distance Running Races." JAMA , 2025 — RACER 2: 29,311,597 finishers, 2010–2023; 176 arrests (0.60/100,000); deaths 0.20/100,000; case fatality 34% vs 71%; men 1.12 vs women 0.19; marathon 1.04 vs half-marathon 0.47; coronary artery disease the most common identified cause. jamanetwork.com · Summary: Northwestern Medicine · NEJM Journal Watch Kim JH, Malhotra R, Chiampas G, et al. "Cardiac Arrest during Long-Distance Running Races." New England Journal of Medicine , 2012 — RACER 1: 10.9 million race finishes, 2000–May 2010; 59 arrests (0.54/100,000); deaths 0.39/100,000. PubMed BMJ Heart blog summary Lee D-c, Pate RR, Lavie CJ, et al. "Leisure-Time Running Reduces All-Cause and Cardiovascular Mortality Risk." Journal of the American College of Cardiology , 2014 — 55,137 adults, mean 15-year follow-up: −30% all-cause, −45% cardiovascular mortality, ~3-year estimated life-expectancy difference; associations seen even at 5–10 min/day at slow speeds. PubMed Pedisic Z, et al. "Is running associated with a lower risk of all-cause, cardiovascular and cancer mortality…" British Journal of Sports Medicine , 2020 — meta-analysis, 14 reports from six cohorts, 232,149 participants: −27% all-cause, −30% cardiovascular, −23% cancer mortality. PubMed Siscovick DS, Weiss NS, Fletcher RH, Lasky T. "The Incidence of Primary Cardiac Arrest during Vigorous Exercise." NEJM , 1984 — relative risk during vigorous exercise 56 (low habitual activity) vs 5 (highest habitual activity); overall risk 0.40 in the habitually vigorous vs sedentary. PubMed Tunstall Pedoe DS. "Marathon Cardiac Deaths: The London Experience." Sports Medicine , 2007 — London Marathon 1981–2006, 650,000 completed runs, cardiac death rate about 1 per 80,000 finishers. PubMed Practical exercise safety: American Heart Association, 2020 scientific statement. Summary and warning symptoms . Method note: RACER figures cover US marathons and half-marathons and count arrests during the race or within an hour of finishing; rates use race finishes as the denominator, not unique people. The registry may miss unreported cases, and findings from US races do not directly establish risk at an Indian event. Sex and race-distance rates use imputation for missing case data. "Expected" values in the race-size panel are simple rate × field-size averages, not predictions for any individual event. This story is data journalism, not medical advice — for personal risk, talk to your doctor. Built from the RACER registry and the studies named above. Adapted from the Muse story, with factual and medical-risk wording reviewed and corrected on 5 November 2026.

title: The Motel That Many People Built: A Front Desk Money Story
body: A story for curious fifth graders, inspired by Kelly Yang’s Front Desk. Explore ownership, stock markets, loans and loan sharks, the history of borrowing, limited liability, and double-entry bookkeeping. Book-ending spoilers ahead.

search_text: The Motel That Many People Built · A Front Desk Money Story Ranjan's linked blog · Young thinkers Read • Try • Explain A money story inspired by Kelly Yang's Front Desk The motel that many people built. One family cannot buy a motel alone. What if a whole community owns little pieces of it? For curious fifth graders About 15 minutes + experiments ⚿ BIG IDEAS SMALL SHARES Welcome, future owner. ROOM FOR EVERY QUESTION Book checkpoint: this story reveals the ending of Front Desk . Mia Tang's family runs the Calivista Motel before they get a chance to buy it. The community's investment is our starting point. The experiments below use made-up teaching numbers unless marked “In the book.” 1. Own a piece 2. Trade a share 3. Borrow carefully 4. Travel in time 5. Limit the risk 6. Keep the books 7. Check out The story and worked examples are readable without JavaScript. Turn JavaScript on to use the sliders, buttons and quizzes. 1 The community becomes the owner A share is a piece of the business. In the book · Chapter 63 Mia imagines finding 600 people who can each contribute $500 : enough for the $300,000 purchase. That is her plan, not a final list of 600 equal owners. In the story, people contribute different amounts. [1] Imagine a business as a giant cake. A share is a slice of its ownership. Owning a motel share does not mean owning Room 7 or getting free stays. It means having a claim on part of the business, with rights set by its rules. An investor puts money into something hoping to earn more later. Investors also take a risk: their shares can lose value, even all their value. Experiment 01 · Build your ownership Our classroom motel has 600 equal shares at $500 each . Together they raise $300,000 . Each square below is one share. How many shares do you buy? 6 1 share 60 shares $3,000 Your investment 1% Your ownership 6 / 600 Your pieces / all pieces Your shares • Pale squares belong to other owners. How did the motel do this year? Earned $12,000 profit Earned $30,000 profit Lost $6,000 Revenue is money earned from guests. Profit is revenue minus the costs of earning it. For this model, the owners keep half of any profit in the business and share the other half as a dividend . The motel pays out $6,000. Your 1% share of that is $60 . It keeps $6,000 for future needs. Classroom model, not the novel's ownership agreement. Dividends are not promised. Actual voting rights, payouts and share classes can differ. For the arithmetic, imagine profit is available in cash after all costs. Try this: move from 6 shares to 12. Your cost, ownership and dividend double. Now choose a loss. Ownership is a share of the risk, too. [2] 2 Ownership can change hands Who gets the money when a share is sold? Mia's plan helps explain raising money by selling ownership . A stock market adds another idea: people can buy and sell shares they already own. A private motel is not automatically listed on a stock exchange. Experiment 02 · Follow the dollars A new share An owner's resale Buyer You → Money goes to The motel company Initial sale · $500 per share Company receives $500 The company creates and sells a share. Your $500 helps buy the motel. This is a primary-market transaction. Imagine a buyer and seller agree on this price: $100 $900 One hypothetical share, bought originally for $500. No fees or taxes. Private ownership may have transfer restrictions or no willing buyer. The slide bar illustrates a negotiated price, not a real market forecast. A stock exchange is an organized place for trading listed shares. Buyers and sellers judge future profits and risks differently. Their orders help set prices. A higher resale price does not put extra cash into the company's bank account. If you sell a share for more than you paid, the difference is a capital gain . Sell for less and you have a capital loss . Worth thinking about: the building can be exactly the same today, while people change what they will pay for its future. [3] 3 A promise has a price Borrowing buys time. Say the motel needs a new washing machine today, but its next guests pay next month. A loan lets it use money now and repay later. The borrowed amount is the principal . Interest is a charge for using it. An owner “I own part of the business. My reward depends on how it does.” A lender “You owe me repayment under our agreement.” A loan does not normally give the lender ownership. A struggling business still owes its debt; a lender can also lose money if it cannot collect. Experiment 03 · When interest earns interest Borrow $1,000 at 10% per year . Suppose you make no payments until the end. Compare two invented agreements. How long before repayment? 3 years 1 year 5 years Simple $1,300 Compound $1,331 Total debt, including the original $1,000. Both bars use the same scale: $0–$1,650. Simple interest adds $100 each year. With yearly compounding, unpaid interest joins the amount that earns interest. After 3 years, that costs $31 more . Show me the arithmetic Simple: $1,000 + (3 × $100) = $1,300. Compound: $1,000 × 1.1 × 1.1 × 1.1 = $1,331. Illustration only. No fees, repayments or changing rates. Real loans may require regular payments and compound on different schedules. In the book · Near the ending Mr. Yao claims someone offered $50,000 more. Mia's parents nearly borrow from loan sharks to fill the gap. Jason reveals that the competing offer is a bluff. The family turns down the dangerous loan and buys the motel for $300,000. [1] A loan shark is a lender who uses unlawful or abusive practices, often with huge charges, hidden terms or threats. An expensive loan deserves scrutiny, but a high rate alone does not tell us whether a lender is breaking the law. The rules depend on the place. “10%” is not enough information. Ten percent per month is very different from ten percent per year. At 10% per month, a $1,000 balance with no payments grows to about $3,138 in one year if interest compounds monthly. At 10% per year, compounded yearly, it becomes $1,100 . Before borrowing, adults should check: How much arrives? How much must be repaid? When? What fees and penalties apply? An annual percentage rate, or APR , helps compare yearly borrowing costs by including interest and certain fees. Threats, pressure to sign quickly and unclear terms are warning signs. Children should bring money worries or threats to a trusted adult. [4] [5] 4 A very old human problem Before bank apps, there was barley. People have needed something today and promised to return it tomorrow for thousands of years. A loan might be grain to plant, silver for trade, or money for a business. These are a few milestones, not a single invention story. About 1780 BCE · A loan on clay A surviving Mesopotamian tablet records a barley loan. People could write down a promise long before credit cards. Other ancient records include loans with interest, loans without it, and rules about repayment. [6] [7] 1494 · A useful system reaches print Luca Pacioli publishes an explanation of double-entry bookkeeping in Venice. Merchants already used the method. He helped spread it; he did not invent it. We'll try it in a moment. [8] 1602 · Many investors, tradable pieces The Dutch East India Company (VOC) raises money from many investors. Trading its shares helps develop an early stock market in Amsterdam. Its investor register survives today. This financial innovation also funded a company involved in colonial violence and exploitation; a clever money tool does not make a business fair. [13] 1855 · An English milestone in limiting risk The Limited Liability Act helps more company investors limit their exposure to business debts. It is one legal milestone, not the worldwide birth of limited liability. Laws and business forms developed differently across countries. [9] 1916 · A push for safer small loans A model Uniform Small Loan Law in the United States aims to move small loans toward licensed, regulated lenders. Different states adopt their own laws. Reformers are trying to answer a hard question: how can people who need small loans get credit without being exploited? [14] Today · The old promise has new rules Banks, credit unions and other lenders make loans under different rules. Consumer protections and disclosures can help borrowers compare costs, but unfair lending has not disappeared. The ancient questions remain: Who owes what, when, and on what terms? Why charge interest? A lender gives up use of the money for a while and risks not getting it back. Prices may also rise over time. Those reasons help explain interest; they do not make every charge fair. Money tools work best when people understand the terms and have real choices. 5 The business has its own pocket Limited liability is a boundary. Liability means legal responsibility. With limited liability , owners generally do not have to use their personal money to pay the company's debts just because they own it. They can still lose what they invested. In the United States, an LLC is a “limited liability company,” a particular legal business form. Its owners are usually called members . A corporation has shareholders and can also offer limited liability. An LLC and a stock-market company are not the same thing. [10] Experiment 04 · Two pockets, one boundary Imagine you invest $500 in a properly run limited-liability business. You also keep $2,000 of personal savings. Later the business fails, owes money and has nothing left. Ordinary owner Owner promises to repay Investment at risk $500 Can be lost Personal savings $2,000 Generally protected The investment can be wiped out. But being an owner alone generally does not make you pay the company's remaining debts from personal savings. Invented example, not the Calivista's legal structure. Personal guarantees, an owner's own wrongdoing and other legal exceptions can change the result. Rules vary by place; this is a basic explanation, not legal advice. A personal guarantee is a separate promise: “If the company cannot repay, I will.” Signing one can put personal assets at risk. Limited liability also does not protect someone from responsibility for their own fraud. The boundary encourages investment, but it is not a permission slip to harm others. [11] 6 Trust needs a record Every transaction tells two sides. Once many people put money into a motel, everyone needs clear records. Double-entry bookkeeping records each transaction in at least two accounts, with equal total debits and credits . Here those words mean the left and right sides of the accounting record, not “bad” and “good.” The central balance is: ASSETS · what it has $0 = LIABILITIES · what it owes $0 + EQUITY · owners' claim $0 Equity is the leftover claim after subtracting liabilities from assets. It is not necessarily cash, and book values are not the same as a company's market price. Experiment 05 · You are the bookkeeper Start a tiny, imaginary motel business. Add six transactions in order and watch the balance above. These amounts are separate from our $300,000 share example. 1. Owners invest $1,000 Reset the books The books start empty. What changes when the owners put in $1,000? Double-entry transaction journal, in dollars Transaction Debit · left Credit · right No entries yet. Tap the green button. Cash $0 · Equipment $0 · Loan owed $0 · Owner investment $0 · Profit $0 Debits and credits are directions. Debits increase assets and expenses. Credits increase liabilities, equity and revenue. A debit can increase one type of account and decrease another, so neither word simply means “money in” or “money out.” Read the complete worked example Owners invest $1,000: debit Cash $1,000; credit Owner capital $1,000. Borrow $500: debit Cash $500; credit Loan payable $500. Buy a $300 washing machine: debit Equipment $300; credit Cash $300. Earn $200 from a guest's completed stay, paid now: debit Cash $200; credit Room revenue $200. Pay a $50 electricity bill for this period: debit Electricity expense $50; credit Cash $50. Repay $100 of loan principal: debit Loan payable $100; credit Cash $100. Finish: Cash $1,250 + Equipment $300 = Loan owed $400 + Equity $1,150. The $150 profit is $200 revenue − $50 expense. The loan was never revenue; repaying its principal was never an expense. Simplified bookkeeping example: no tax, interest, depreciation or other costs. Revenue and expenses flow into equity through profit. Equipment is shown at purchase cost here; its cost can become an expense over time through depreciation. Two surprises: borrowing raises cash but creates an equal debt, so it does not create profit. Buying a washing machine swaps one asset for another; it does not make $300 of value vanish that day. Balanced books help spot mistakes, but even balanced entries can contain wrong information. [12] 7 Before you hand back the key Can you run the front desk? Try these four questions. A wrong answer is a useful place to learn. 1. You own 12 of 600 equal shares. What fraction of the company is yours? 12% 2% 50% 2. You sell your old share to a friend for $650. Who receives the $650? You, the seller The motel company 3. The motel borrows $500. Has it earned $500 of profit? Yes No 4. Does limited liability mean your $500 investment cannot be lost? Yes, it is safe No, it can be lost 0 of 4 ideas unlocked. Try the questions again The biggest idea A business is more than its money. Mia's community brings trust, work and hope as well as investment. Shares describe who owns what. Loans describe who owes what. Limited liability helps define the risk. Bookkeeping makes the promises visible. Talk about it: If a motel makes a profit, how should its owners balance repairs, fair pay, lower room prices and dividends? Arithmetic can show the trade-offs. People still have to choose. Source desk Book scenes are paraphrased; all artwork and classroom examples are original. Checked November 6, 2026. The story explains ideas, not an investment recommendation. Book facts and the “13,000 shares” question [1] Kelly Yang, Front Desk (Arthur A. Levine Books / Scholastic, 2018), especially Chapter 63 and the closing chapters. The $300,000 purchase and the $50,000 bluff are also described in this chapter summary . Publisher’s classroom guide. The figure “13,000 shares” could not be verified in the book, so it is not used as a book fact here. Mia's 600 × $500 plan is distinguished from the varied contributions in the ending. Our equal-share company, its dividends, trades, legal form and accounting entries are invented teaching models. Finance, history and accounting references U.S. SEC Investor.gov: Stocks . The 1916 model small-loan law and subsequent regulation. All the assumptions behind the experiments Share model: 600 identical shares; $500 initial price; investment = shares × $500; ownership = shares ÷ 600. Positive profit pays a 50% dividend, divided in proportion to ownership. A loss pays no dividend in this model. Trade model: one existing share, initially bought for $500. Gain or loss = resale price − $500. No fees, taxes or extra shares issued in the resale. Loan model: $1,000 principal, 10% annually; simple total = $1,000 × (1 + 0.1 × years); annual compound total = $1,000 × 1.1 raised to the number of years. No payments or fees. Monthly comparison: $1,000 × 1.1 raised to 12 = $3,138.43. Liability model: a passive owner who paid for the investment in full, with no separate promise to repay, wrongdoing or other exception, versus an owner who gives a personal guarantee. Accounting model: transactions are recorded when the described service or purchase happens, with cash paid immediately. A small selection of accounts keeps the example readable. Totals are carried exactly and currency displays are rounded to cents where needed. A book can open a door. A good question can keep it open. title: Colorado 2026: The Whole Ballot
body: An interactive guide to Colorado’s 2026 election: all 14 statewide measures, statewide offices, Congress, the legislature, boards and judges. Unofficial Nov. 5 vote snapshot, with the Nov. 6 AP call in District 3 and publication corrections noted inside.

search_text: Colorado 2026 Election Results — The Full Ballot General election · Tuesday, November 3, 2026 Colorado statewide ballot Compiled Nov. 6, 2026 Colorado 2026: the whole ballot , not just the winners Every statewide measure with what it would have done and where it stood in the count, every statewide office, the Senate race, all eight U.S. House districts, the legislature's before-and-after party math, the boards and the judges — 14 ballot measures were split 7–7 between passing and failing , while Democrats swept the statewide offices and U.S. Senate race and stand to take two-thirds supermajorities in both chambers of the legislature. Unofficial results — nothing here is certified Vote figures retain the Muse story’s reported Secretary of State snapshot, compiled by Rocky Mountain Voice as of 6:25 p.m. MST, Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026 , with original call labels from that snapshot except CD-3, updated to AP’s Nov. 6 call. This is a dated snapshot, not a live results feed. Ballots cured for signature/ID problems and military/overseas ballots can still arrive through Nov. 12; state certification is Nov. 30. Publication update · Nov. 6, 2026: This inline edition preserves the original vote-count snapshot. It updates AP’s call for Jeff Hurd in CD-3, corrects threshold and recount arithmetic, clarifies provisional outcomes and board-seat math, and repairs the statewide-office table. Sources and verification limits . 2,618,500 ballots counted in the Nov. 5 snapshot — 64.05% of active voters; all 64 counties reported 7 – 7 statewide ballot measures passing vs. failing, out of 14 4 of 4 statewide offices won by Democrats — all open seats, all by 17–27 points 7–1 possible U.S. House delegation, from 4–4, if the Democratic lead in CD-4 holds; AP has called six for Democrats and one for Republicans +7 projected legislative gains, Republican → Democratic, if all Nov. 5 leads hold; none projected the other way 1 U.S. House race still uncalled by AP on Nov. 6: the 4th (D leading) Party scorecard Ballot measures Statewide offices U.S. Senate U.S. House State legislature Boards & judges Still open · what's next Questions & answers Sources § 1 What each party actually did The split personality of the night: Democrats won the statewide offices, the U.S. Senate race and most U.S. House seats, while several conservative citizen initiatives passed anyway. Voters separated the people from the policies. Democrats Won the people — offices, Congress, legislature Swept all four statewide offices — Governor, Attorney General, Secretary of State, Treasurer — each an open seat and a Democratic hold, by 17 to 27 points. Re-elected Sen. John Hickenlooper by 24.7 points. Flipped two Republican U.S. House seats — CD-5 (Colorado Springs, first Democrat ever to win it) and CD-8 — and lead in a third, CD-4, where Lauren Boebert trails. On Nov. 5 leads: 7 gains, no losses: +1 in the Senate (24–11) and +6 in the House (49–16) on current leads — two-thirds supermajorities in both chambers. Held their existing board seats: all three CU Regent seats; State Board of Education retains a Democratic majority: 5–4 if Wright wins CD-3, 6–3 if Clementi wins. On measures: the graduated income tax (Amendment 87) and K-12 funding (Proposition NN) are passing; the 4.4% tax cap (Prop. 136) is failing. Republicans Lost the offices — but won several policy fights Lost all four statewide offices and the Senate race by roughly 25 points. Two House incumbents defeated (Jeff Crank in CD-5, Gabe Evans in CD-8); a third, Lauren Boebert in CD-4, trails in an uncalled race. AP called CD-3 for Jeff Hurd on Nov. 6. Were on course to lose 7 legislative seats and with them the numbers needed to block veto overrides and referred amendments in either chamber. Four conservative propositions were passing: Prop. 132 (fentanyl penalties), Prop. 133 (life without parole for trafficking a minor — the biggest Yes of the night at 62.15%), Prop. 134 (school sports by biological sex) and Prop. 135 (barring sex-altering surgery on minors). But all six Republican-backed constitutional amendments were below their passing threshold — Amendments 81–86 — and the income-tax cap, Prop. 136, was trailing while Amendment 87’s graduated tax was leading. Uncalled measures remain provisional. § 2 All 14 statewide ballot measures The part of the ballot that changes the law. Amendments 81–86 would add language to the state constitution, so each needed 55% Yes — a threshold Amendment 85 was below despite a Yes majority. Amendment 87 and all seven propositions needed only a simple majority. Thirteen of the 14 were citizen-initiated; only Proposition NN was referred by the legislature (Senate Bill 26-135). Yes 44.96% 1,145,731 No 55.04% 1,402,744 One of six citizen-initiated constitutional amendments below 55% in this snapshot. The only measure referred by the legislature (Senate Bill 26-135); the other 13 were citizen initiatives. Proposition 137 Passing · uncalled Proposition · needs a majority Close Let the state keep and spend sporting-goods sales-tax revenue above the TABOR limit — about $175 million a year from July 1, 2027 — as a voter-approved revenue change for water, land and forest conservation, wildfire prevention and outdoor recreation. Why is it marked failing? Because of the 55% rule. Since 2016, any amendment that adds language to the Colorado constitution needs 55% Yes, not a bare majority. Amendment 85 (plain-language ballot questions) has 51.17% Yes to 48.83% No in this snapshot — a lead of 59,445 votes — but is 3.83 points below the threshold . That is why it is marked failing rather than passing. It was uncalled in the original snapshot, and remaining ballots can change the totals. Then why did Amendment 87 — also a constitutional amendment — need only a majority? The 55% rule applies only to amendments that add language. The Secretary of State lists Amendment 87 as requiring a simple majority because it works by repealing the constitution's single-rate income-tax requirement rather than adding new language. In this snapshot, Amendment 87 is above its threshold at 51.20%, while the rival tax cap, Proposition 136, is below its threshold at 47.37%. Both were uncalled; these are not certified outcomes. Which passing measure had the smallest Yes–No vote gap? Amendment 87 , the graduated income tax: Yes leads by 60,866 votes (51.20%–48.80%). Next is Proposition 137 (conservation funding from sporting-goods tax revenue) at 74,054 votes, then Proposition 135 at 107,499. Amendment 85 has a smaller Yes–No gap (59,445) but is below its separate 55% passing threshold, so a Yes–No gap alone does not rank how close a constitutional measure is to passing. At the other extreme, Proposition 133 drew the highest Yes share of the night — 62.15% — and Amendment 84 (mail-ballot ID numbers) the lowest, 36.82%. Is Lauren Boebert's race over? Not officially. AP had not called CD-4 as of Nov. 6: Eileen Laubacher (D) leads Boebert 184,103 (48.75%) to 181,079 (47.95%) with about 97% of the vote counted. The 3,024-vote lead is about three times the automatic-recount threshold (~920 votes), so no recount is triggered unless the margin collapses as cure and overseas ballots are counted through Nov. 12. Boebert had not conceded in any Colorado source indexed as of Nov. 6. How did Republicans lose the statewide offices while four conservative measures were passing? Because measures aren't candidates. Props. 132–135 were citizen initiatives decided on their own merits, and each drew majority support — 52–62% Yes — from an electorate that simultaneously voted 59–61% Democratic for governor and senator. The pattern has a limit, though: when conservative ideas were packaged as constitutional amendments needing 55%, all six were below that threshold in the snapshot, and the tax cap (Prop. 136) was trailing too. Uncalled measures remain provisional. Voters picked Democratic people and a mixed bag of policies. What does a legislative supermajority actually let Democrats do? Two things mainly: override a governor's veto and refer constitutional amendments to the ballot , both of which take two-thirds of each chamber. In the Senate, 24 of 35 meets the two-thirds threshold; the Nov. 5 projection includes the then-uncalled Democratic leads in SD-11 and SD-30. In the House, 49 of 65 clears the 44-seat bar with room to spare. Note the practical catch: Governor-elect Weiser is himself a Democrat, so veto overrides matter less than the amendment-referral power — which provides a legislative route to put future constitutional amendments before voters.
